surprises.head: Laurent Brossoit stole one
surprises.body: Brossoit allowed 2 goals on 33 shots, worth 4.6 expected goals: 2.6 fewer than expected. That is more than Anaheim’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 30 starts.

surprises.head: Anaheim’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Anaheim’s power play has been near the bottom of the league for years. Not tonight: 3 power-play goals on 4 chances. A power play like theirs against a kill like Pittsburgh’s scores 3 or more about once every 25 games.

story.head: Gauthier lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Mikael Granlund opened the scoring for the Ducks on the power play midway through the first. Cutter Gauthier scored early in the second and again less than three minutes later to make it 3-0. The third period was a wild one. Tristan Luneau extended the lead to 4-0 on the power play early in the period. With the goalie pulled, Kris Letang got the Penguins on the board on the power play just under three minutes later. With the goalie still pulled and a little over six minutes left, Rickard Rakell cut Anaheim’s lead to 4-2 on the power play. Gauthier completed his hat trick into the empty net with 34 seconds left. Gauthier’s goals came one on the power play, one at even strength and one into an empty net. Granlund assisted on all three. Jackson LaCombe finished with three assists.

The score flatters the Ducks: the Penguins had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Penguins win about six in ten. Laurent Brossoit was the difference, stopping 31 of 33. Artūrs Šilovs stopped 20 of 24 for the Pens.

The Ducks went 3-for-4 on the power play. The Ducks killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes early in the second. The Ducks moved to 10-7-1 and climbed to third in the Pacific, while the Penguins fell to 6-10-2, seventh in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Ducks are rolling: five straight wins.
Cutter Gauthier has a point in eight straight games, with a goal in each of the last six.
The Ducks have beaten the Penguins four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.

The Ducks won without Troy Terry, A.J. Greer, Ian Moore and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Penguins were missing more at the time.
